title: Kuala Lumpur/North
wikitext:
{{pagebanner|Gombak Selangor Batu-Caves-01.jpg|origin=-1,0|pgname=North Kuala Lumpur|unesco=yes}}
[[Kuala Lumpur]]'s '''Northern Suburbs''' is the huge area running north of the [[Kuala Lumpur/Central|City Center]] and [[Kuala Lumpur/Tuanku Abdul Rahman|Tuanku Abdul Rahman]]'s Chow Kit area. It is largely residential and industrial and will not be of particular interest to the visitor, except for the famous limestone cave temples of '''Batu Caves'''.

Other attractions which may draw visitors are the '''Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM)''' which has a huge green reserve with a canopy walk, and the National Zoo (''Zoo Negara''). For something more unusual, there is also the '''Orang Asli Museum''' in Gombak which showcases the culture and lifestyle of Peninsular Malaysia's Orang Asli or indigenous groups.

==Do==
===Sport===
*'''Rock climbing''' at Batu Caves - This limestone outcrop 13 km from the city centre offers a great variety of [[Rock climbing |climbing]] on steep limestone routes. Over one hundred bolted lines contain features similar in nature to those found in [[Rai Leh]], Thailand. Easy access from downtown and a simple street-level approach makes for a convenient and challenging day of climbing.
